title: Compliance Macro Plan & Risk Signal Tracker for SOC2/ISO Cutovers
creator: Liam Chen
description: High-level macro plan to coordinate SOC2 and ISO cutover activities across Product, Engineering, and Security. This ticket captures a lightweight milestone timeline, automated risk signals to watch during cutover windows, decision log for trade-offs (evidence sampling vs full ingest), and a playbook for escalating anomalies detected in audit log delivery or SSO provisioning. The goal is to create a single source of truth for stakeholders so cutovers are predictable and non-blocking to revenue teams.
acceptance_criteria: Central milestone timeline published and linked to per-team runbooks
Risk signal dashboard (green/amber/red) implemented and exercised in two dry-runs
Rollout gating checklist defined and approved by Security and Legal (signed PRD)
Evidence collection flow for audit logs validated end-to-end (ingest -> retention -> retrieval)
milestones: 2026-03-10: Kickoff with Engineering and Security; alignment on retention and KMS boundaries
2026-03-18: Finalize SSO cutover plan (SSO toggle + fallback); publish canary schedule
2026-04-01: Implement risk-signal producer in Console (error-rate, backlog, delivery-lag)
2026-04-12: First dry-run: ingest sample audit logs from staging; validate queries and retention
2026-05-10: Production cutover weekend (staged rollout with A/B lanes)
recent_activity: 2026-03-02: Shane (Eng) posted prototype metrics for audit log lag (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4821)
2026-03-05: Design review with Nora: new retention UI flagged for later sprint; added to dependencies
2026-03-08: Product review: shifted canary window from 03-25 to 04-01 to give Eng additional runway
2026-03-11: Security asked to add HSM KMS mapping for private customers (added to dependencies)
decisions: Use staged evidence sampling (10% -> 50% -> 100%) during rollouts to minimize immediate SRE load
Prioritize signed audit log delivery (S3 + CloudTrail-style index) over enriched metadata in initial cutover
Canary lanes will be region-based (us-west-2 then us-east-1) to test routing and KV cache behavior under real traffic
outstanding_risks: Audit-log backlog: prolonged backfill could push retention costs beyond budget if not throttled
SSO provider token expiry edge-case causing orphaned sessions during toggle
Customer migration scripts for legacy audit formats lack automated validation leading to schema drift
Insufficient observability for quantization/serving-level errors when private deployments use older runtime

(Owner: Shane) Add error-budget gating hook into risk-signal producer (estimate: 3 points)
